title: simple-dispatcher: a parked or failed session's status is the last thing it posts, even with tool activity relayed
description:
Repo: JKershaw/simple-dispatcher

## Goal

When a session parks (defer, blocked) or fails, its park or terminal status is the last thing it posts, so that Harbour reads the park correctly.

## Why

`hook.js`'s comments say `statusLast` keeps the park or terminal status "genuinely the final entry" (`hook.js:399-403`, `1957-1961`). But with `SD_TOOL_ACTIVITY_RELAY=1`, defer, blocked and failed post the `kind:'tool'` entry **after** the status. That was checked with `driveStopHook`: `defer → [assistant-text, status:[pending]…, tool:Read…]`. Harbour's `parseParkedWait` (`lib/session-telemetry.js:324`) reads the latest entry and skips only decision stamps, so a trailing tool entry hides the park. The flag defaults to off, so production doesn't hit this today. It would as soon as tool activity is relayed. Two Surveys of LIN-4218 found it; LIN-4218 preserves today's order on purpose (a refactor), so the fix is here.

**After LIN-4218**, whose single table of outcome orders makes this a one-slot change.

## Done when

* With every relay flag on, defer, blocked and failed post their status last. A test fails if any relay follows it.
* Harbour reads the park from such a session, shown against Harbour's reader or its contract.

## Report back

What changed · what was left, and why · what still looks fuzzy · follow-ups, listed rather than filed.

## How to go about it (from a Survey before work began)

Two Surveys at simple-dispatcher `bf499a4` (on LIN-4150) agree on the fix and differ on the proof:

* **The code change is one slot in three rows.** In `STOP_OUTCOMES`, move `'A'` ahead of `'S'` in defer, blocked and failed (complete already ends `…A, E, M, S`), and remove the `statusLastTrailingTool` exception from the table comment, `EXCEPTIONS` and the `T < S < A` assertion. A name left in `EXCEPTIONS` with no row using it fails nothing, so remove it on purpose.
* **The golden breaks on purpose:** about 28 TOOL-on rows re-record (order and the cursor snapshot at the S post). Review the diff by hand; it should hold only those swaps.
* **The golden has no row for the case Harbour actually reads.** Only `parseParkedWait` (LinearViewer `lib/session-telemetry.js:324`) reads the park by position, and only for `/scheduled wakeup/i`, which comes only from the structural async-wait defer. None of the golden's defer rows contains it.
* **For blocked and failed, Harbour already reads correctly:** `findWakeEvent` and `deriveTerminalStatus` scan backwards. The change is order hygiene there, not a reader fix. Say so.
* **"Last" can still break from outside this process:** reapers.js can post a marker after the park, and `render-run-steps.js:334` notes that a trailing `[usage]` entry defeats `parseParkedWait` too.
* **Don't add a third hand-rolled "status is last" check** (`ticket-marker-relay.test.js`'s F1 case already has one, with only the marker relay on).

### Scope decision (4 Nov, about 21:45 UTC)

John asked Claude to take the human's role in this process and to err on the side of larger tidies. **The decision: fix the order in the hook, and make Harbour read a park the one way it reads every other park, so the read no longer depends on what posts last.** In pieces:

1. **simple-dispatcher: the order, as a table rule.**
   * First, a failing test: add a scheduled-wakeup defer case to the golden (all three relay flags on), and a table rule that every row which posts and isn't status-first ends in `S`. Replace F1's hand-rolled check with the rule, or make F1 use it.
   * Then swap the three rows, remove the exception, delete the stale `statusLast` comment (`hook.js` \~177-182), regenerate the golden, and confirm the diff is only the swaps and the new rows.
   * **Prove it against Harbour's reader,** not a copied regex: feed the `driveStopHook` feedback for the scheduled-wakeup defer to `parseParkedWait`, as LIN-4187's contract tests do.
2. **Harbour: one way to read a park** (its own piece, after 1). `parseParkedWait` scans back past entries that aren't status (tool activity, `[usage]`, stamps), the way `findWakeEvent` does, so a trailing entry from any process can't hide a park. A unit test with a trailing tool entry and a trailing `[usage]` entry, red before and green after. If the two readers can share the backward scan, share it.

**At merge (we'll check it):**

* with every flag on, no relay follows the status in defer, blocked or failed, and a test fails if one does;
* the golden diff holds only the swaps and the new rows;
* Harbour reads the park from the scheduled-wakeup defer, shown with Harbour's own reader;
* **who else must learn about it:** the note at `render-run-steps.js:334`, the cross-process caveat in `postTicketMarkerDelta`'s comment, and any doc that calls the park status "the final entry" now describe what's true.

**Not this task's:** decision scanning in outcomes that never do it; sharing the sequence with `opencode-runner.js`; splitting `main()`'s effects.

---

*Filed by [Claude Code](<https://claude.ai/code>) for the Survey research*

## Implementation Plan

*Pruned at close-out (5 Nov 2026). The full plan (rev 2, with the B1 revision) is preserved in the task snapshots and the comment trail.*

**Implemented as approved, in two pieces:**

* Piece 1, LIN-4239, simple-dispatcher: PR [https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/326](<https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/326>) (`796bc9d`). defer, blocked and failed now post their status last; status-last table rule; `defer-scheduled-wakeup` golden row; `test/system/park-read.test.js`. Comment follow-ups: PR #327 (`580a5ea`) and PR #328 (`07c88f7`).
* Piece 2, LIN-4240, LinearViewer: PR [https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2280](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2280>) (`279dcb0a`). `parseParkedWait` reads the newest state-bearing entry, skipping stamps, `tool`/`usage`/`resources`, legacy `[usage]` and `[ticket]` lines.

Deviations: none from the approved plan. Additions: `kind:'resources'` in the reader's skip set and a heartbeat guard (review notes 1 and 2); a retry-budget witness test.

Session fit: needs multiple sessions

plan-review due: yes
(kept word for word from the approved plan; the plan was approved and the work has landed.)

comments.body:
### Plan Review Verdict

**Verdict:** Request Changes — piece 1 is sound and ready to build, but piece 2's reader design still lets the reaper's trailing `[ticket]` marker hide a park. That is the cross-process hole the plan says it closes, and the plan would write a comment claiming it is closed.

Blocking findings: 1

**What I checked** (simple-dispatcher `bf499a4` and LinearViewer `476d9ad4`, both still HEAD of `origin/main`; nothing has landed on the touched files since the ticket was filed):

- `STOP_OUTCOMES` (`hook.js:467-476`) and `runStopOutcome`: the three rows read exactly as the plan says. Moving `A` before `S` is a one-slot change per row. The `failed` case posts nothing after `relay()`, and defer/blocked hold only *after* the row has run, so nothing else lands after the S post from this process.
- `stop-relay-table.test.js`: `EXCEPTIONS` and the `T < S < A` assertion are where the plan says. `decision-emission.test.js:131-143` asserts the hazard as "documented". F1 (`ticket-marker-relay.test.js:346`) has its own `last.kind === 'status'` check.
- Golden: 7 affected rows (defer ×3, blocked ×3, failed ×1) × 4 TOOL-on flag sets = 28. `BASE` carries a Bash tool pair, so every TOOL-on row really does post a tool entry. None of the existing defer rows reaches the structural async-wait defer, so the new `defer-scheduled-wakeup` row is needed. The status it produces (`hook.js:1516-1531`) is `[working · verifying] Not done yet — a scheduled wakeup still pending…`, which is the only shape `PARKED_WAIT_HINT` matches. That defer is `holdable:false`, so the row won't enter a hold.
- Harbour: `parseParkedWait` (`lib/session-telemetry.js:324`) is the only reader that goes by literal last position. Its other consumers read `telemetry.parkedWait`. `findWakeEvent` and `deriveTerminalStatus` scan backwards, as the plan says. `tool` and `usage` are in `FEEDBACK_ENTRY_KINDS`, so the `kind` the new skip depends on survives ingest. The drift test constraint (`decision-lifecycle-stamp-drift.test.js:141-157`) is as described.
- The premise holds: the producer table is where the bad order comes from, and the reader's last-entry dependency is a real second cause. The plan is right to fix both and to keep `findWakeEvent` separate (the two readers return different things).

---

**B1 (blocking): piece 2 does not close the `[ticket]`-marker hole it cites, and the plan would write a false comment saying it does.**

The plan sets aside "fix the producer only" because that "leaves the cross-process hole F2 already measured". F2 is `reapers.js` posting a duplicate `[ticket] LIN-… done` *after* the park. But reapers posts that marker with `kind: 'status'` (`reapers.js:310`), and piece 2 deliberately keeps any `status` entry decisive. Built as written, a trailing reaper marker still hides the park. The plan then rewrites the F2 comment block (`ticket-marker-relay.test.js:433-440`) to say the residual "now only hides the park from an old reader". That sentence would be false, and so would the `postTicketMarkerDelta` caveat the ticket's at-merge list asks to make true.

This matters to the task. The Scope decision's goal for piece 2 is "a trailing entry from any process can't hide a park", and the reaper is the other process.

**Change:** describe the skip set as "entries that are not a statement about the session's state": stamps, `kind` `tool`/`usage` (plus the legacy untagged `[usage]`), **and ticket-marker lines**. Recognise a ticket-marker line with the module's own `TICKET_PREFIX` (`lib/session-telemetry.js:258`) rather than a new regex. A `[ticket]` line is lane bookkeeping, and a session that genuinely moved on also posts text, tool or status lines. Add one witness, red before and green after: a park, then `{kind:'status', message:'[ticket] LIN-1 done'}` → still parked. Keep the "park followed by `[done]` / heartbeat / `assistant-text` → not parked" guards. Write the F2 comment and the `postTicketMarkerDelta` caveat to match what is built.

*Alternative*, if the team prefers to keep `status` decisive: keep piece 2 as it is, but say plainly in the F2 comment, the `postTicketMarkerDelta` caveat and the plan's follow-ups that a trailing reaper marker still hides a park. Then drop the F2 hole from the reasons given for piece 2. I recommend the skip: it is one more predicate, and leaving the marker out leaves exactly the hole the ticket named.

---

**Notes for the builder (not blocking)**

1. **The Harbour proof is not "as LIN-4187's contract tests do".** No system test imports a Harbour module today. LIN-4187's tests (`d8d186c`) talk to a running Harbour over HTTP. `test/system/park-read.test.js` will be the first to `import()` from `HARBOUR_DIR`. Use `pathToFileURL(path.join(process.env.HARBOUR_DIR, 'lib/session-telemetry.js')).href`. Note that `session-telemetry.js` pulls in `workspace.js` → `providers/registry.js` / `connection-binding.js`. Harbour's own unit suite imports it without a DB, so it should load, but confirm that on the first run rather than assuming it.
2. **`deriveTerminalStatus` returns null for `[blocked]`**: `[blocked]` is not a terminal marker. For blocked, assert `findWakeEvent(feedback).marker === 'blocked'` (or `deriveBlockedStatus` / `deriveLifecycleStatus`, `lib/dispatch-terminal.js:254-269`). For failed, assert `deriveTerminalStatus(feedback) === 'failed'`.
3. **The new golden row's freshness:** `resolveAsyncWait` drops waits older than `maxAgeMs`. Give the trailing `ScheduleWakeup` line a timestamp that is fresh against the hook's `now` (or check that a missing `ts` counts as fresh). Keep the row's own precondition asserting `hook.action === 'defer'` and the full status. The plan already has this; it is the guard that the row reaches the structural branch at all.
4. **The shared order helper should take a list of posted bodies (`{kind, message}`) plus an outcome type,** not a `driveStopHook` result. F1 records through `runHookTurn`, and the golden through its own stub, so a body list is what both have.
5. **More stale "latest entry" text to update with piece 2:** the `routes/dashboard-feed.js:180-184` comment ("only from the run's own latest feedback text (…parseParkedWait)"), and `parseParkedWait`'s own docblock ("Only the LATEST feedback entry decides"). Both fall under the plan's description, so this is a note.
6. **Retry budget (the plan's risk 2):** confirmed. `terminalPostRetryOptions` measures against `HOOK_STARTED_AT`, so tool posts now spend wall-clock that `[failed]`/`[blocked]` used to have first. The plan's "read it and report, don't reorder" is the right handling.
7. **Golden review:** besides the 28 swaps and 8 new rows, expect the per-POST session snapshot on the moved tool entries to be unchanged and the S snapshot to show the advanced `toolActivity.cursor`. Anything else is a finding, as the plan says.

**Hand-off:** back to `plan` for B1. Piece 1 can go to implementation unchanged once B1 is settled. If you split the plan, piece 1 is approvable as written.

### Plan revised (answers the Plan Review Verdict)

**B1 — fixed.** Confirmed at `reapers.js:310`: the reaper posts the `[ticket]` marker with `kind:'status'`, so keeping `status` decisive would have left the hole piece 2 claims to close. `parseParkedWait` now skips entries that are not a statement about session state: stamps, `tool`/`usage` kinds, a legacy untagged `[usage]`, and ticket-marker lines (matched with the module's own `TICKET_PREFIX`). Witness added, red before and green after: park then `{kind:'status', message:'[ticket] LIN-1 done'}` is still parked. Guards added: park, marker, `[done]` is not parked. The F2 comment and `postTicketMarkerDelta` caveat are now listed to be written to match what is built.

**Notes 1-7 — all taken:** (1) the Harbour import is flagged as the first of its kind, with `pathToFileURL` and a first-run check; (2) blocked is asserted via `findWakeEvent(...).marker === 'blocked'`, failed via `deriveTerminalStatus`; (3) the new row gets a fresh `ScheduleWakeup` timestamp; (4) the shared helper takes a list of `{kind, message}` bodies; (5) `dashboard-feed.js:180-184` and the `parseParkedWait` docblock are added to the stale-text list; (6) the retry-budget check is kept as read-and-report; (7) golden review expectations are explicit.

Piece 1 is unchanged. Still `needs multiple sessions`, `plan-review due: yes` (piece 2 changed, so it wants a second read). The description holds the one current plan, replaced in place.

### Plan Review Verdict

**Verdict:** Approve. B1 is answered and the answer holds. Piece 1 is unchanged and still right. Piece 2 now closes the reaper-marker hole without letting a finished or progressing session read as parked.

**What I checked** (simple-dispatcher `bf499a4` and LinearViewer `476d9ad4`; both are still `origin/main`, and nothing has landed on the touched files since the ticket was filed):

- **B1.** `reapers.js:303-312` posts each transcript `[ticket]` block with `kind:'status'`, so skipping by message (not by kind) is the only way to close the hole, and the revised plan does that. `TICKET_PREFIX` (`lib/session-telemetry.js:258`) is non-global, so reusing it with `.test()` is safe. It matches the walk's six states. A line it doesn't match stays decisive, which errs toward "not parked" (the safe side). Witness 4 (park → `[ticket] LIN-1 done` → parked) and the guard "park → marker → `[done]` → not parked" are the right pair.
- **Over-skip risk (the plan's risk 3).** Heartbeats stay decisive, which is correct. For a scheduled-wakeup park, the reaper's idle beat is `[working · verifying] verifying in background (scheduled wakeup) · idle …`: `verifyTask` is `'scheduled wakeup'` (`heartbeat.js:264`, `hook.js:2014-2015`), so it still matches `PARKED_WAIT_HINT` and extends the park. A beat with real tool activity (`[working · <cat>] N tools…`) correctly ends it. The guards in witness 6 keep this true.
- **Piece 1** is as last reviewed. `STOP_OUTCOMES` is at `hook.js:467-476`, the `statusLastTrailingTool` comment is at `hook.js:458-460`, and the `parseParkedWait reads only the latest` claim is at `hook.js:465-466`. The 28 + 8 golden expectation stands.
- The drift-test constraint (`_isStampEntry(` must stay in `parseParkedWait`) is handled by letting the new predicate call it.
- Not sharing the scan with `findWakeEvent` is well argued: the two readers return different things.

**Notes for the builder (not blocking)**

1. **Add `kind:'resources'` to the skip set.** It is inside the plan's own description ("not a statement about the session's state") but missing from its list. With `SD_RESOURCE_RELAY=1`, `reapers.js:271-288` posts `[resources] {…}` on every heartbeat-interval tick. The heartbeat itself backs off (`tickSession` returns no message until `nextPostAt`, up to 10 min). So a parked session gets `[resources]` entries trailing the park between beats, and today they hide it. That is the same shape as the tool relay: off by default, and it bites when the flag goes on. Add it to the predicate, give it a witness beside 1–2 (park → `kind:'resources'` → parked), and include it in the docblock wording. The remaining `FEEDBACK_ENTRY_KINDS` (`dispatch-store.js:99`) are decided as follows: `evidence` posts before `S` (complete only), `recap` comes only from the opencode runner (out of scope), and `refusal` stays decisive, which is the safe default.
2. **Optional extra guard for witness 6:** park, then the reaper's awaiting-verify heartbeat `[working · verifying] verifying in background (scheduled wakeup) · idle 2m · next heartbeat in ≤1m` (`kind:'heartbeat'`), which should stay parked with `latest` advanced. This pins the production shape that keeps heartbeats decisive and safe.
3. **Re-run the plan's own search** (`grep -n "kind: 'status'" reapers.js hook.js`) and also grep for `kind: '` in `reapers.js`/`heartbeat.js`. The `resources` case above was found that way, and the plan's "every place" search only looked at `status`.
4. **`render-run-steps.js:325-336`:** the stale note names "trailing-`[usage]`" and says the fix "is tracked separately". Rewrite the whole parenthetical, not just the trailing sentence, since this task is that fix.

**Hand-off:** on to `implementation`. Piece 1 goes first (simple-dispatcher PR, with the golden diff reviewed by hand and the system-tier `park-read.test.js` proof), then piece 2 (LinearViewer PR). Two sessions, as the plan says.

### Breakdown

The approved plan (review **Approve**, comment `66095182`, rev 2) has been split into its two pieces. Re-grounded before splitting: simple-dispatcher `origin/main` is still `bf499a4` and LinearViewer `origin/main` is still `476d9ad4`. `git log --since` the ticket's creation shows nothing on the touched files except LIN-4218's own `bf499a4`, which is the plan's grounding commit. The `STOP_OUTCOMES` rows (`hook.js:467-476`), `TICKET_PREFIX` (`:258`) and `parseParkedWait` (`:324`) are where the plan says. No drift, so no re-plan.

| Order | Subtask | Repo | Blocked by |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **LIN-4239**: defer, blocked and failed post their status last (table rule, shared helper, `defer-scheduled-wakeup` golden row, swap, system-tier `park-read.test.js` proof) | simple-dispatcher | none |
| 2 | **LIN-4240**: `parseParkedWait` reads the newest state-bearing entry, skipping stamps, `tool`/`usage`/`resources`, legacy `[usage]` and `[ticket]` lines; witnesses 1–6; stale-text rewrites | LinearViewer | LIN-4239 |

**Why two pieces (the plan's session-fit reason):** two repos, two PRs and two CI runs. Each is verified on its own: piece 1 by the hand-reviewed golden diff (28 swaps + 8 new rows) and the system-tier proof against Harbour's own reader, piece 2 by Harbour's unit suite. Piece 1 lands first because its proof must go red and then green on the producer swap alone, against today's reader. Each subtask says it fits one session and carries `Plan-review due: no`, citing this approval.

**What's folded in from the approving review:** LIN-4240 adds `kind:'resources'` to the skip set with a witness (note 1), the scheduled-wakeup heartbeat guard (note 2), the `kind: '` census grep (note 3), and the rewrite of the whole `render-run-steps.js:325-336` parenthetical (note 4).

**One engineering choice made at breakdown:** the plan puts `postTicketMarkerDelta`'s caveat and the F2 comment in piece 1, but the behaviour they describe lands in piece 2. Written as the plan words them ("no longer hides it from the current reader"), they would be false between the two merges. So LIN-4239 writes them to be true at its own merge: a trailing marker hides a park from a latest-entry reader, and Harbour skips markers from LIN-4240 on. LIN-4240's acceptance includes confirming they are true once it lands, with a one-line simple-dispatcher follow-up if the wording needs it.

**Piece 1 (LIN-4239) report.** PR https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/326 (f50679c). CI result follows on LIN-4239.

**What changed:** the table swap (defer `U C M T A S`, blocked `U C M T D A S`, failed `U C M T A S`), statusLastTrailingTool removed everywhere, the status-last table rule with a shared helper, a defer-scheduled-wakeup golden row, `test/system/park-read.test.js`, and comments and docs rewritten to what holds at this merge.

**Retry budget (plan risk 2), confirmed and reported, not reordered around:**
- Production (FOLLOWUP_HOLD_MS default 3600000): the hook timeout is 3660 s, so the terminal budget is min(start+3655 s, now+60 s) = now+60 s. It does not depend on how long the tool relay took. A failed or blocked stop with 300 tool lines still gets its retry; `test/stop-status-retry-budget.test.js` witnesses this and goes red with retries disabled.
- Exposure, hold disabled (FOLLOWUP_HOLD_MS=0, hook timeout 20 s, status window 15 s): the tool relay now runs before the status, so a relay that runs past the window leaves the status one attempt. Reproduced in a scratch run with a shrunk window: 1 [failed] POST instead of 2. At 60 ms per tool POST it takes about 250 relayed lines to reach the 15 s window. Whether any real config sets hold to 0 is not verified here.

**Plan vs code:**
- The S post's status kind is not always `status`: a refusal-classified block posts `kind:'refusal'`. The shared helper accepts both; the plan did not mention it.
- Open question answered: resolveAsyncWait never ages out a ScheduleWakeup (the wake path skips the cutoff), so a missing ts counts as fresh. The golden row still sets a timestamp.
- The system proof's failed case first used a wait-bearing transcript, so the structural defer beat the FAILED sentinel. That was a fixture error, fixed before the swap. Existing behaviour is unchanged.
- Harbour import: session-telemetry.js loaded on the first run with no setup, so nothing was stubbed.

**Left, and why:** a reaper [ticket] marker from another process can still hide a park from Harbour's newest-entry reader until LIN-4240 lands. This piece's comments state that.

**Fuzzy:** whether any production config sets FOLLOWUP_HOLD_MS=0. The window exposure above depends on it.

**Follow-ups, listed not filed:** decide whether a hold-0 config is supported, given the window exposure; LIN-4240 (sibling reader fix).

## Review — LIN-4233

Reviewed piece 1, simple-dispatcher PR https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/326 at head `f50679c` on base `bf499a4`, which is still `origin/main`. PR state: open, mergeable, CLEAN. Piece 2 (**LIN-4240**, LinearViewer) is **Todo**: nothing has been built there yet. LinearViewer `origin/main` is still `476d9ad4`. (The distilled brief says piece 1 is "approved and merged". It is neither. That line is stale.)

CI: green. The `unit tests` check (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `npm test`) passed on `f50679c`. The system tier is not in CI; see the ledger.

### What I checked myself

- **Scope vs plan.** The files touched match piece 1's places in the plan. The only extra is `test/stop-status-retry-budget.test.js`, which is the witness for plan risk 2. There is no overrun.
- **Table.** defer `U C M T A S`, blocked `U C M T D A S`, failed `U C M T A S`. `statusLastTrailingTool` is gone from the comment, the rows, `EXCEPTIONS` and the `T<S<A` assertion. There is no stale `statusLast` text on `postTurnText`.
- **Golden diff, checked by script, not by eye.** 28 rows changed, all of them TOOL-on (`…A1`). In each, the only change is that the status event moves after the tool event(s), and the only state change is on the S event, which gains `toolActivity.cursor`. Tool events' state is unchanged. 8 rows were added (`defer-scheduled-wakeup` × 8). 0 rows were removed. Every TOOL-off row is byte-identical. This holds the at-merge "only the swaps and the new rows" check.
- **Re-ran:** the 5 affected unit files pass 60/60. `test/system/park-read.test.js` with `HARBOUR_DIR` at LinearViewer `476d9ad4` passes 3/3. Harbour's `session-telemetry.js` loads with no setup.
- **Mutation (LIN-2274).** I put the three rows back to the old `…S A` order. The following went red: the table rule, the golden "records every row" precondition (`statusLastViolations`), the golden match, the decision-emission `[blocked]`-last test, both retry-budget tests, and park-read's **scheduled-wakeup defer** case. As the plan predicts, park-read's blocked and failed cases stay green under the mutation, because Harbour's `findWakeEvent`/`deriveTerminalStatus` already scan backwards. Those two are order hygiene, as stated. Mutation reverted; worktree clean.
- **Regression.** `git log` on the touched files shows no revert and no earlier order fix that this undoes. LIN-4218 (`bf499a4`) is the base.
- **Siblings (class: "a post can follow the park/terminal status").** All in-process producer rows are now covered by one rule. The cross-process writers in `reapers.js` are `:285` `resources`, `:310` `[ticket]` as `kind:'status'`, and heartbeats. These are the reader's job and are bounded into LIN-4240's skip set. The opencode runner is out of scope per the ticket. No other instance is unhandled.

**Non-blocking (no fix required):** `test/helpers/stop-status-order.js` `statusIndex` treats the *last* non-marker `status`/`refusal` body as the outcome's status. A stray status-kind post after the real S would therefore be read as "the status", and the violation would be masked. Today the structural table rule covers this, so the gap only matters if a future row adds a second status-kind post.

### What CI Did Not Prove

- **Inside** (the Scope decision's piece 2: "one way to read a park", where a trailing entry from any process can't hide it). **LIN-4240 must land.** That means `parseParkedWait` skips stamps, `tool`/`usage`/`resources`, the legacy `[usage]` line and `TICKET_PREFIX` lines, with witnesses 1–6. Witness 4 (park → `{kind:'status', message:'[ticket] LIN-1 done'}` → parked) must be red before and green after, and the guard (park → marker → `[done]` → not parked) must hold. The Harbour stale text must also be rewritten: `lib/session-telemetry.js:307` docblock, `lib/render-run-steps.js:325-336`, `routes/dashboard-feed.js:180-184`, `docs/dispatch-integration.md:503-507`. Settled by LIN-4240 merging with Harbour CI green, not by filing anything, because it is already this ticket's own subtask. **LIN-4233 must not be marked Done before then.** #326 can merge on its own.
